summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Cellular respiration is a stepwise catabolic oxidation of organic substrates yielding 30–32 ATP per glucose molecule (ΔG°' = -2870 kJ/mol).

conceptBreakdown.content:
Cellular respiration is the enzyme-catalyzed, stepwise catabolic oxidation of organic respiratory substrates (carbohydrates, fats, proteins, organic acids) within living cells, liberating energy in the form of Adenosine Triphosphate ($\text{ATP}$):

$$\Large \mathbf{\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 + 6\text{O}_2 \longrightarrow 6\text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Energy } (30\text{--}32\text{ ATP} / \Delta G^{\circ \prime} = -2870\text{ kJ/mol})}$$

- **Stepwise Energy Release**: Respiration does not release energy in a single explosive thermal step; rather, energy is captured in discrete packets via metabolic phosphorylation cascades into $\text{ATP}$.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PLANT GAS EXCHANGE STRUCTURES
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                             ▼                             ▼
     STOMATA                       LENTICELS                 PNEUMATOPHORES
  Microscopic epidermal pores   Lens-shaped periderm openings  Negatively geotropic breathing
  in leaves & green stems.      in woody stems & roots.       roots in halophilic mangroves.
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Stomata**: Microscopic pores bounded by guard cells in the epidermis of leaves and herbaceous green stems that facilitate rapid diffusive gas exchange ($\text{CO}_2$ influx and $\text{O}_2$ efflux).
- **Lenticels**: Loosely packed, suberin-free complementary cells rupturing through the cork/phellem layer of woody stems and perennial roots.
- **Pneumatophores**: Negatively geotropic respiratory root extensions with lenticels in halophytes (*Rhizophora*, *Avicennia*) enabling oxygen uptake in waterlogged, anoxic saline mud.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Why Plants Lack Specialized Respiratory Organs
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Why Plants Lack Specialized Respiratory Organs
conceptBreakdown.content:
Unlike animals that possess specialized lungs, gills, or tracheal systems, plants have no localized respiratory organs due to three key evolutionary and anatomical features:

1. **Autonomous Organ Gas Exchange**: Each plant organ (leaf, stem, root) takes care of its own gas-exchange needs with minimal transport of gases between distant parts.
2. **Low Volumetric Gas Demand**: Plant tissues have substantially lower metabolic rates compared to active animals. During daylight, photosynthetic leaves produce internal $\text{O}_2$ at rates far exceeding respiratory demands.
3. **Loose Parenchyma Packing & Intercellular Spaces**: Interior living parenchyma cells in leaves, stems, and cortex are loosely arranged with an extensive network of intercellular air spaces, ensuring that virtually every living cell is in direct diffusion contact with ambient air.
